questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Passengers may ride in a caravan if it is being towed slowly.
Passengers may ride in a caravan only if it has seats fitted and seatbelts.
It is always illegal for passengers to ride in a caravan on a public road.

questions.explanation: Passengers may not be carried in a caravan being towed on a public road.

questions.question: You see this combination sign. What does this sign mean?

options.text: Only hatchback vehicles are prohibited from stopping; other vehicles may stop.
Stopping is allowed for hatchbacks only if passengers are entering or exiting.
No vehicle may stop in this area for any reason, including loading or unloading.

questions.explanation: No-stopping sign with a light-motor-vehicle plate; the video's answer is that no vehicle may stop there for any reason, including loading or unloading.

questions.question: Under which condition is it legally permissible to tow another vehicle on a public road?

options.text: If the towed vehicle’s driver is holding any valid driver’s licence.
If the driver of the towed vehicle is holding a licence that authorizes them to drive that class of vehicle and maintains control of the steering wheel.
If the towing is done slowly and the road is quiet, no licence requirements apply.

questions.explanation: The person steering a towed vehicle must hold a licence for that class of vehicle and must control the steering.

questions.question: You see a road sign showing this icon. What is the correct meaning of this sign?

options.text: There is a golf course ahead; watch out for pedestrians crossing and slow-moving golf carts.
Only golfers may enter this area; all other traffic is prohibited.
Vehicles must stop and give way to anyone playing golf in the area.

questions.explanation: Golf course ahead: watch for pedestrians and slow golf carts crossing.

questions.question: A breakdown vehicle is towing another vehicle on a public road. What is the maximum legal speed allowed?

options.text: 60 km/h
80 km/h
100 km/h

questions.explanation: The video gives 80 km/h as the maximum speed for a breakdown vehicle towing another vehicle.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding passengers on the roof of a vehicle on a public road?

options.text: Passengers may sit on the roof if the vehicle is moving slowly in a residential area.
Passengers or animals may never occupy the roof while the vehicle is in motion.
Passengers may sit on the roof if the vehicle is not exceeding 40 km/h.

questions.explanation: No person or animal may be carried on the roof of a moving vehicle.

questions.question: You see a green road sign with the words “3-Phase.” What does this sign indicate?

options.text: There are three lanes ahead, each with separate traffic phases at the traffic light.
The traffic light ahead operates on a three-phase system; wait until the signal is green.
There are three roads converging ahead; proceed with caution.

questions.explanation: A '3-Phase' information sign means the traffic signal ahead is a three-phase signal; wait for your green.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about a vehicle’s electrical wiring and battery is correct when driving on a public road?

options.text: A vehicle may be driven even if the battery terminals are loose, as long as the headlights work.
Exposed wiring is allowed if it does not touch the driver or passengers.
All electrical wiring and the battery must be properly installed, insulated, and secured before driving on a public road.

questions.explanation: Wiring and the battery must be properly installed, insulated and secured.

questions.question: You see the road marking “SOS” painted on the lane. What does this marking mean?

options.text: It is a warning zone; vehicles may not stop or park under any circumstances.
It is an emergency area; you may stop or park only in an emergency.
All vehicles may stop here to check directions or make a phone call.

questions.explanation: 'SOS' painted on the road marks an emergency stopping area; stop there only in an emergency.

questions.question: You see a road marking indicating an “arrestor bed” ahead. What is the correct action for drivers?

options.text: Slow down slightly; the arrestor bed is decorative and for visual guidance only.
Stop immediately; the arrestor bed is a pedestrian crossing.
Be prepared to enter the arrestor bed only in an emergency, such as brake failure, to safely stop the vehicle.

questions.explanation: An arrestor bed is for emergencies such as brake failure.

questions.question: You see this command sign on a public road. What does this sign require you to do?

options.text: Switch on your headlights only at night or when visibility is poor.
Switch on your headlights only if you are driving outside a built-up area.
Switch on your headlights immediately and keep them on while travelling in the indicated area.

questions.explanation: Blue command sign showing headlights: switch on headlights and keep them on in the indicated area.

questions.question: You see this command sign on a public road. What does this sign require you to do?

options.text: Switch off your headlights immediately and continue driving without them while in the indicated area.
Keep headlights on if it's dark or raining; the sign is just a recommendation.
Only switch off your high beams; keep dipped beams on.

questions.explanation: This is the headlight command sign crossed out; the video's answer is that you must switch off your headlights in the indicated area.

questions.question: Which of the following must your car be properly equipped with when driving on a public road?

options.text: A speedometer that is in good working order.
A radio and air conditioning.
Only tyres and brakes; speedometer condition does not matter.

questions.explanation: A vehicle must have a speedometer in good working order.

questions.question: In which of the following scenarios are you legally allowed to stop your vehicle in a no stopping zone?

options.text: To quickly drop off a passenger.
To wait for a friend to join you.
Only if a situation beyond your control forces you to stop, such as a mechanical failure or sudden illness.

questions.explanation: In a no-stopping zone you may only stop for reasons beyond your control.

questions.question: Who is responsible for ensuring that all passengers in a vehicle are wearing seatbelts while the vehicle is in motion?

options.text: Only passengers over 18 years old are responsible for themselves.
The driver of the vehicle is responsible for all passengers.
Parents or guardians are only responsible for children under 12, the driver has no responsibility.

questions.explanation: The driver is responsible for passengers wearing seatbelts.

questions.question: You see a road sign with the top half showing “60” and the bottom half showing a visibility warning. What does this sign mean?

options.text: The speed limit is always 60 km/h, regardless of visibility.
The speed limit is recommended only in foggy conditions, otherwise normal speed limits apply.
You must reduce your speed to 60 km/h because poor visibility conditions are expected or present.

questions.explanation: Speed limit with a poor-visibility (fog) plate: 60 km/h applies when visibility is poor.

questions.question: You see a stop/go traffic sign being used by a traffic officer or temporary road controller. What must you do?

options.text: Ignore the sign if the traffic light ahead is green.
Stop or go according to the signal given by the traffic officer, even if it conflicts with normal traffic lights or signs.
Proceed with caution; the sign is only a recommendation.

questions.explanation: Stop/go signs held by an authorised person override traffic lights and other signs.

questions.question: You see this combination road sign. What is the correct interpretation?

options.text: You must reduce your speed only at the first curve; afterwards you may drive at the normal speed limit.
You may ignore the speed restriction if the road looks clear.
You must maintain the indicated speed limit for the entire 6 km stretch of winding road.

questions.explanation: The speed limit applies for the whole distance shown on the plate (6 km of winding road).

questions.question: Which of the following are you allowed to do under normal circumstances?

options.text: Stop in a no-stopping zone to quickly drop off a passenger.
Exceed the speed limit briefly while overtaking another vehicle.
None of the above.

questions.explanation: You may not stop in a no-stopping zone to drop off a passenger, and you may not exceed the speed limit while overtaking.

questions.question: When requested by a traffic officer, within what time must you produce your driving licence in order to avoid a fine?

options.text: Within 24 hours at the nearest police station.
Within 7 days from the date of the request.
Immediately, when requested by the traffic officer.

questions.explanation: You must produce your driving licence immediately when a traffic officer asks for it.

questions.question: What is the name of the group of signs to which these signs belong?

options.text: Regulatory signs
Command signs
Warning signs

questions.explanation: Triangular red-bordered signs (including yellow temporary ones) are warning signs.

questions.question: How far ahead should your vehicle’s high beams and dipped beams be able to illuminate the road?

options.text: High beams: 60 m | Dipped beams: 30 m
High beams: 80 m | Dipped beams: 40 m
High beams: 100 m | Dipped beams: 45 m

questions.explanation: High beams must illuminate 100 m ahead and dipped beams 45 m.

questions.question: You see a road sign showing a green arrow pointing downwards above a lane. What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must change lanes immediately.
The lane is reserved for emergency vehicles only.
You may drive in this lane.

questions.explanation: A green downward arrow above a lane (lane-control signal) means you may use that lane.

questions.question: A learner driver is not allowed to do which of the following?

options.text: Drive a motor vehicle without exceeding the speed limit.
Drive on a public road while accompanied by a licensed driver.
Leave the engine running while the vehicle is unattended.

questions.explanation: No driver may leave a vehicle unattended with the engine running.

questions.question: When driving on a road with a painted island, under which condition are you allowed to drive on or stop on the painted island?

options.text: When traffic is heavy and you need extra space to pass other vehicles.
When making a U-turn or avoiding a slow-moving vehicle.
Only when directed to do so by a traffic officer.

questions.explanation: You may not drive or stop on a painted island unless directed by a traffic officer.

questions.question: For how long is a vehicle licence valid?

options.text: 6 months from the date of issue.
12 months from the date of issue.
5 years from the date of issue.

questions.explanation: A vehicle licence (disc) is valid for 12 months.

questions.question: You see this combination sign. What does this mean?

options.text: The speed limit of 100 km/h applies at all times.
You may exceed 100 km/h during the day if visibility is good.
The night speed limit of 100 km/h applies only from sunset to sunrise.

questions.explanation: A speed limit with a night-time plate applies only from sunset to sunrise.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding driver fatigue?

options.text: If you feel a little tired, you may continue driving as long as traffic is light.
Drinking coffee or energy drinks eliminates the need to rest while driving.
If you have been driving for a while and you are feeling a little tired, stop and have a break.

questions.explanation: If you feel tired, stop and rest.

questions.question: You see a reservation sign indicating a pedal cycle lane. What is the correct meaning?

options.text: Only bicycles may use this lane; all other vehicles are prohibited.
Pedestrians and cyclists may use the lane.
Vehicles may drive in the lane if there is no cyclist present.

questions.explanation: A pedal-cycle reservation sign reserves the lane for bicycles only.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the use of a hooter on a public road?

options.text: You may use the hooter continuously to warn other drivers of your presence.
You may use the hooter to express annoyance at another driver’s behaviour.
You may use the hooter only when it is necessary to warn other road users of danger.

questions.explanation: Use the hooter only when necessary to warn others of danger.

questions.question: You see a combination road sign applying to a light motor vehicle. What does this sign indicate?

options.text: The maximum speed a light motor vehicle may travel at on this road.
The recommended speed for light motor vehicles in good weather conditions.
The minimum speed a light motor vehicle must travel at.

questions.explanation: A blue circular speed sign is a minimum speed command sign; with the light-motor-vehicle plate it applies to light motor vehicles.

questions.question: You are not allowed to drive a light motor vehicle on a public road if:

options.text: It is not fitted with front fog lamps.
It is not fitted with lamps at the rear emitting a red light.
The interior light is not working.

questions.explanation: A vehicle must have rear lamps emitting red light.

questions.question: You see this combination road sign. What does it mean?

options.text: Light motor vehicles may not exceed the speed limit for the next 5 km.
Light motor vehicles are prohibited only at certain times over the next 5 km.
Light motor vehicles are prohibited from using this road for the next 5 km.

questions.explanation: Prohibition sign with a light-motor-vehicle symbol and a 5 km plate: light motor vehicles are prohibited for the next 5 km.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct when entering a public road from a side road, driveway, or entrance?

options.text: Enter the road as soon as there is a small gap and force other vehicles to slow down.
You may enter the road if you indicate, even if other traffic must change speed.
Do not enter a public road if your vehicle will interfere with moving traffic that will approach you from any direction.

questions.explanation: Do not enter a public road if you will interfere with moving traffic.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding parking on a public road is correct?

options.text: You may park near an excavation if warning signs are displayed.
You may park opposite an excavation as long as traffic can still pass.
It is not allowed to park your vehicle near or opposite an excavation.

questions.explanation: You may not park near or opposite an excavation.

questions.question: You see a road marking reserved with a special symbol for ambulances. What does this marking indicate?

options.text: Any emergency vehicle may park here.
Only ambulances may park in this bay.
This is a waiting area for patients or visitors.

questions.explanation: A yellow encircled 'A' marking reserves the bay for ambulances only.

questions.question: Under which of the following conditions are you allowed to overtake another vehicle on the left on a public road?

options.text: When the vehicle in front is turning right and there is space on the left.
When traffic is heavy and you want to save time.
On a single-lane road at night if no other vehicles are coming.

questions.explanation: You may overtake on the left when the vehicle ahead is turning right and there is room.

questions.question: You see a lane reserved for buses and public transport. Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Any vehicle may use the lane if traffic is heavy.
Only buses and vehicles carrying at least 3 passengers may use the lane.
Only buses and authorized public transport vehicles may use the lane.

questions.explanation: A bus reservation lane is for buses and authorised public transport only.

questions.question: When approaching a pedestrian crossing (zebra crossing), which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: You may overtake another vehicle stopped at the crossing if no pedestrians are visible.
You must stop and give way to pedestrians on the crossing, regardless of whether the other vehicle has stopped.
You may speed up to pass the crossing quickly if pedestrians are far away.

questions.explanation: Give way to pedestrians on a crossing; do not overtake a vehicle stopped at a crossing.

questions.question: Which of the following makes a light motor vehicle illegal to drive on a public road?

options.text: Tyres with worn tread below the legal minimum depth.
Tyres with slight discoloration but no visible damage.
Tyres with minor dirt or mud.

questions.explanation: Tyres must have at least the legal minimum tread depth (1 mm).

questions.question: What is the correct name of the road sign that displays destination names and directions, usually in a long rectangular shape pointing toward routes or towns?

options.text: Direction indicator
Guide sign
Fingerboard

questions.explanation: A pointed rectangular sign with a destination name is a fingerboard (direction) sign.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the use of a communication device while driving on a public road is correct?

options.text: A driver may use a communication device if the vehicle is stationary at a red traffic light.
A driver may hold and use a communication device if it is used briefly and safely.
A driver may use a communication device only if it is fitted to the vehicle or can be operated without holding it.

questions.explanation: A communication device may only be used hands-free / when fitted to the vehicle.

questions.question: What does the rocks falling warning sign indicate?

options.text: Loose stones may damage vehicle windscreens.
Rocks may fall onto the roadway from the side of a hill or mountain.
The road surface ahead is uneven due to gravel.

questions.explanation: Falling rocks: rocks may fall onto the road from a hill or mountain side.

questions.question: Which of the following actions is legally permitted when driving on a public road under normal conditions?

options.text: Crossing a solid white line to overtake a slow-moving vehicle.
Driving on the right-hand side of the road when visibility is clear.
Crossing a solid white line in order to avoid an obstruction in the roadway.

questions.explanation: A solid white line may be crossed only to avoid an obstruction (when safe).

questions.question: A minimum speed limit sign is displayed on a public road. Under which of the following circumstances may a driver legally drive slower than the indicated minimum speed?

options.text: When the driver feels uncomfortable driving at higher speeds.
When traffic behind the vehicle is moving slowly.
When road, traffic, or weather conditions make it unsafe to maintain the minimum speed.

questions.explanation: You may drive slower than a minimum speed only when conditions make it unsafe.

questions.question: At an uncontrolled four-way intersection, two vehicles approach at the same time from different directions. Which rule determines who has the right of way?

options.text: The vehicle travelling at the higher speed.
The vehicle approaching from the left.
The vehicle approaching from the right.

questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, yield to the vehicle approaching from the right.

questions.question: You approach an intersection controlled by a yield sign. Another vehicle approaches the same intersection from a different road controlled by a stop sign. Both vehicles arrive at the same time. What must you do?

options.text: Proceed first because a yield sign gives you priority over a stop sign.
Stop completely and proceed only when the intersection is clear.
Proceed with caution, but give way to any vehicle already in or approaching the intersection.

questions.explanation: At a yield sign, give way to vehicles already in or approaching the intersection.

questions.question: Which of the following combinations of flashing lights correctly identifies a vehicle that you are legally required to yield to immediately on a public road?

options.text: Amber flashing lights on a vehicle travelling slowly.
Blue flashing lights on a private security vehicle.
Red or blue flashing lights on an authorised emergency vehicle.

questions.explanation: Yield to authorised emergency vehicles with red (or blue) flashing lights.

questions.question: What does this combination road sign require a driver to do?

options.text: Stop only if pedestrians are already crossing the road.
Slow down and proceed if pedestrians are waiting on the sidewalk.
Give right of way to pedestrians who are on or about to enter the roadway.

questions.explanation: Yield to pedestrians sign: give right of way to pedestrians on or about to enter the road.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding parking near a pedestrian crossing is correct?

options.text: You may park within 5 metres of a pedestrian crossing if no pedestrians are present.
You may park near a pedestrian crossing provided your hazard lights are switched on.
Do not park within 9 metres of a pedestrian crossing.

questions.explanation: Do not park within 9 m of a pedestrian crossing.

questions.question: What does this combination road sign indicate?

options.text: You may not exceed 50 km/h for the next 6 km.
The recommended speed is 50 km/h for the next 6 km.
Drive at a minimum of 50 km/h for the next 6 km.

questions.explanation: Blue minimum-speed sign with a 6 km plate: drive at least 50 km/h for the next 6 km.

questions.question: Are you allowed to overtake another vehicle when approaching a blind bend on a public road?

options.text: No, overtaking is prohibited when approaching a blind bend.
Yes, if you can briefly see oncoming traffic.
Yes, if the road markings allow overtaking.

questions.explanation: Never overtake when approaching a blind bend.

questions.question: What does a temporary “Tunnel ahead” warning sign indicate?

options.text: A permanent tunnel is located ahead on the route.
The road surface ahead is permanently enclosed.
A temporary or provisional tunnel exists ahead, often due to roadworks or construction.

questions.explanation: A yellow (temporary) tunnel warning sign warns of a temporary tunnel, e.g. at road works.

questions.question: What does a red circular road sign with a white horizontal bar across the centre indicate?

options.text: No stopping at any time.
Road closed ahead.
No entry for all vehicles.

questions.explanation: A red circle with a white horizontal bar is the 'No entry' sign.

questions.question: You see this warning sign. What does this mean?

options.text: Vehicles taller than 4.42 metres may proceed if they drive carefully.
The road ahead has a bridge, tunnel, or obstruction and vehicles taller than 4.42 metres may not pass.
Only heavy vehicles are restricted; light vehicles may ignore the sign.

questions.explanation: Height-limit warning (4.42 m): vehicles taller than shown may not pass.

questions.question: Which of the following rules must be obeyed when refueling a vehicle at a petrol station?

options.text: The engine may be left running if the handbrake is applied.
The engine may be left running if refueling is done quickly.
The engine of a vehicle should not be left running while petrol is being pumped into the fuel tank.

questions.explanation: The engine may not run while fuel is being pumped into the tank.

questions.question: What does this road sign indicate?

options.text: U-turns are prohibited at all times.
U-turns are allowed only during daytime hours.
You are not allowed to perform a U-turn during night-time.

questions.explanation: No U-turn with a night-time plate: U-turns are prohibited at night only.

questions.question: Which of the following situations legally requires a driver to stop immediately, even if no road sign or traffic signal is present?

options.text: When a pedestrian is waiting to cross at an uncontrolled intersection.
When a vehicle behind you flashes its headlights repeatedly.
When instructed to do so by a traffic officer or authorised person.

questions.explanation: You must stop when instructed by a traffic officer or authorised person.

questions.question: What does this temporary road sign indicate?

options.text: The recommended speed for all lanes is shown temporarily.
Vehicles in all lanes must maintain the indicated speed at all times.
The right-hand lane has a temporary minimum speed limit.

questions.explanation: Temporary sign showing a minimum speed for the right-hand lane.

questions.question: Which of the following actions is not permitted when your vehicle has broken down ona public road?

options.text: Switching on your hazard lights immediately.
Placing a warning triangle at the prescribed distance behind the vehicle.
Leaving the vehicle unattended in a position that obstructs traffic when it could be moved.

questions.explanation: Do not leave a broken-down vehicle where it obstructs traffic if it can be moved.

questions.question: Which control is used to indicate to other road users that you intend on changing lanes?

options.text: A
B
G

questions.explanation: Diagram: A steering wheel, B indicator lever, C gear lever, D parking brake, E clutch, F brake, G accelerator. B is the indicator lever.

questions.question: In order to make your vehicle move, which controls would you need to use?

options.text: A, B, D
D, F, C, B
C, D, E, F, G

questions.explanation: Diagram: A steering wheel, B indicator lever, C gear lever, D parking brake, E clutch, F brake, G accelerator. Pulling away uses the gear lever (C), parking brake (D), clutch (E), brake (F) and accelerator (G).

questions.question: Which control would you use to turn your vehicle?

options.text: A
G
F

questions.explanation: Diagram: A steering wheel, B indicator lever, C gear lever, D parking brake, E clutch, F brake, G accelerator. A is the steering wheel.

questions.question: Which controls would you use to change from 2nd to 3rd gear?

options.text: E, G
E, A
C, E

questions.explanation: Diagram: A steering wheel, B indicator lever, C gear lever, D parking brake, E clutch, F brake, G accelerator. Changing gear uses the clutch (E) and gear lever (C).

questions.question: Which control prevents your vehicle from rolling once parked?

options.text: D
A
B

questions.explanation: Diagram: A steering wheel, B indicator lever, C gear lever, D parking brake, E clutch, F brake, G accelerator. D is the parking (hand) brake.

questions.question: Which control would increase the speed of your vehicle?

options.text: E
F
G

questions.explanation: Diagram: A steering wheel, B indicator lever, C gear lever, D parking brake, E clutch, F brake, G accelerator. G is the accelerator.

questions.question: Which control would decrease the speed of your vehicle?

options.text: E
F
G

questions.explanation: Diagram: A steering wheel, B indicator lever, C gear lever, D parking brake, E clutch, F brake, G accelerator. F is the brake pedal.

questions.question: Which two controls would you use during an emergency stop?

options.text: F, G
C, D
E, F

questions.explanation: Diagram: A steering wheel, B indicator lever, C gear lever, D parking brake, E clutch, F brake, G accelerator. In an emergency stop use the brake (F) and clutch (E).
